job_description_info.job_description:
# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

company_info.company_description:
Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg, Germany. It builds payment and business tools for small merchants, including card terminals, a point-of-sale app and business accounts. It has also introduced a personal account for merchants’ customers. The company serves millions of merchants across Europe and the Americas and employs around 2,500 people in approximately 20 offices.

Quillstone’s culture emphasises **ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes**, alongside pragmatism, humility, candid feedback and open sharing of context. Teams have autonomy over their services and how they solve merchant problems, guided by shared principles rather than heavy processes.

The company is **office-first**, with teams working together on site most days and agreeing on some flexible days. It supports development through training budgets, peer feedback, internal tech talks and development plans reviewed twice a year. It also offers relocation support for many roles, supports local business education and publishes an annual inclusion report.

With six years in analytics and data science, including more than four as a data scientist, I bring experience building models used by operational teams and translating business questions into actionable analyses.

At Thistlebox, I built a LightGBM model to forecast weekly demand for individual recipes, using calendar features to support ingredient ordering. The model reduced forecast error from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%. I also built an XGBoost churn propensity model used to target retention offers and evaluated its uplift using a holdout set. Alongside this work, I write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.

The opportunity to work with engineers, data scientists and product managers also aligns with the practical, team-based work described in the role.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my modelling, evaluation and analytics engineering experience could contribute to your Customer Support AI team. Thank you for your consideration.

Yours sincerely,

Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
